title: iPSC-Astrocyte Differentiation Protocol
author: Charlie Arber
materials: Passage glial progenitors before they reach 100% confluence.
Feed cells twice per week with maturation media.

steps.title: Coat plasticware with Geltrex
steps.instruction: Dilute Geltrex 1:100 in DMEM‑F12, add to the desired vessel (e.g., 6‑well plate, T25/T75 flask), incubate 1 hour at 37 °C, then remove excess before seeding.

steps.title: Generate cortical neurons
steps.instruction: Follow the published Shi et al. Nat Protocols (PMID 22976355) to differentiate iPSCs into cortical neurons and culture them until day in vitro (DIV) 60–80.

steps.title: Passage glial progenitor cells
steps.instruction: Remove growth media, wash once with PBS lacking Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺, add 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS and incubate 4–5 minutes at room temperature; carefully aspirate EDTA, then force‑wash cells off with fresh glial progenitor media (N2B27 + 10 ng ml⁻¹ FGF2) while pipetting up/down ≈5 times over the whole growth area; seed the suspension onto the freshly Geltrex‑coated vessel at a split ratio of 1 : 3 to 1 : 5 (≈25,000 cells cm⁻²) in glial progenitor media.

substeps.instruction: Wash once with PBS without Mg and Ca.
Add 0.5 mM EDTA in PBS; incubate 4–5 min at RT.
Wash cells off with N2B27 + 10 ng ml⁻¹ FGF2, pipetting ≈5 times.
Seed at 1 : 3–1 : 5 split ratio (~25,000 cells cm⁻²).

steps.title: Maintain glial progenitors
steps.instruction: Culture glial progenitor cells, splitting them once or twice per week as needed; they can be maintained and passaged for >1 year, although proliferation often slows after DIV 200.

steps.title: Monitor astrogenic switch
steps.instruction: Around day 115 observe the transition from neuronal morphology (small round soma) to glial morphology (larger, flatter, less defined soma); by day 150 (passage > 15) the astrogenic switch is considered complete and cells are ready for astrocyte maturation.

steps.title: Mature astrocytes
steps.instruction: Replace media with Astrocyte maturation media containing BMP4 and LIF; culture for at least 2 weeks (do not exceed 4 weeks) to allow maturation, noting reduced cell division after BMP4+LIF addition.

steps.title: Activate astrocytes
steps.instruction: Treat mature astrocytes for 16 hours with IL‑1α (3 ng ml⁻¹), TNFα (30 ng ml⁻¹) and C1q (400 ng ml⁻¹).

steps.title: Cryopreserve GPCs
steps.instruction: At any stage after maturation, suspend cells in N2B27 medium containing 10 % DMSO and freeze using standard cryopreservation procedures.

description: Take validation steps such as glutamate uptake, phagocytosis, response to inflammation (nuclear NFkB by ICC, C3 protein production, inflammatory cytokine production by qPCR or ELISA) can be tested to provide evidence of astrocytic identity. Calcium imaging can be used to measure astrocyte functional responses.
